# Spotify
A Python Spotify workflow in the style of Alfred’s built-in Music Mini Player: playback above, keyboard browsing on the left, artwork on the right.
Requires **Alfred 6 with Powerpack**, **Python 3.14+**, and the **Spotify desktop app**. No pip packages, PHP runtime, background service, or separate installer.
**[Clear Connection](alfred://runtrigger/com.aqsnow.alfred.spotify/clear-connection/)** clears saved authorization and pending sign-in. Your Client ID and Client Secret stay configured. The browser opens for a fresh sign-in the next time you launch the player. This action is also available here in **Configure Workflow**.
## Install
Build with `./build.sh`, then open `dist/Spotify.alfredworkflow` and import it into Alfred. If Python is missing, install it with `brew install python`.
Type **`spotify`** in Alfred. On first use, connect your Spotify account as described below. The workflow reuses music metadata and artwork already cached by the Spotify desktop app; the first cache scan runs in the background.
## Connect your library
There are just two workflow settings: **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.
1. Create an app in the [Spotify Developer Dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard). Set its redirect URI to **`http://127.0.0.1/spotify_callback`** (without a port) and enable the Web API. Each sign-in uses a dynamically assigned local port. Spotify requires a loopback IP address; `localhost` is not accepted. 2. Paste its Client ID and Client Secret into this workflow’s configuration. 3. Open `spotify`. Sign-in opens automatically when both credentials are present. Approve access in your browser, then return to Alfred.
Missing credentials open a setup screen. A failed or cancelled sign-in shows an error with **Try Again** and **Workflow Settings** actions. The player stays on the connection screen until authorization succeeds. Initial sign-in is automatic. If you close the browser tab before finishing, reopen the player and choose **Connect** to open a fresh sign-in tab. This recovery button disappears after you connect successfully.
To set a global launch shortcut, open **Alfred Preferences → Workflows → Spotify** and double-click the **Hotkey** object labelled **Launch Spotify Mini Player**. Press your preferred key combination and save it. No shortcut is pre-assigned, so importing the workflow does not replace another app’s hotkey.
Tokens refresh automatically. Spotify currently requires the owner of a Development Mode app to have Premium. Additional users must be allowed in that app’s dashboard. See Spotify’s [development-mode rules](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/concepts/quota-modes). The workflow never asks for your Spotify password.
## Use
| Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `↑` / `↓` | Select a row and preview its artwork | | `↩` | Browse the selection or play a track | | `⌘1` … `⌘9` | Open one of the first nine rows | | Type | Filter the current view; search cached music from the home view | | `⌫` at the end of a folder path | Go up one folder | | `⌘[` | Go back, or clear the current filter | | `⌘R` | Refresh the desktop cache index and connected library | | `⌘,` | Open workflow settings | | `⌃⌘↓` | Play / pause | | `⌃⌘←` / `⌃⌘→` | Previous / next track |
Use **Search Spotify for …** at the end of home search results to search the full catalog. Local searches do not call the Web API. Playback uses the Spotify desktop app and stays in the player. A configurable launch hotkey is available in Alfred’s workflow editor.
## Cache behavior and limits
- Spotify’s desktop cache is **read-only**. A small SQLite index contains the names, Spotify URIs, and file offsets needed for browsing. The original HTTP cache is not copied. Only artwork that is displayed is extracted into a file Alfred can load; existing cached artwork is preferred over a download. - Library membership comes from the public API after connecting. Previously cached metadata and artwork are reused to avoid unnecessary requests. The full library refreshes at most daily, or when you press `⌘R`. - The adapter understands Chromium Simple Cache v5 and Spotify’s cached JSON and protobuf music metadata. Missing, evicted, truncated, or unknown formats fall back to available indexed data and the public API. - Spotify no longer supplies genres in its desktop metadata. Genres appear only when your followed-artist API responses contain them; unavailable tags are not invented. Star ratings are not supported by Spotify. - Spotify’s current API only returns playlist contents to the owner or a collaborator. Other playlists can still be opened or played. - Client credentials stay in Alfred’s local workflow configuration. OAuth tokens are in a user-only file in this workflow’s data folder. Neither is included in the built workflow. The callback listens only on `127.0.0.1`, validates OAuth state, and closes after completion or three minutes.
The workflow does not read Spotify cookies, extract login tokens, or download or decrypt cached audio. It calls only the public Spotify Web API and public artwork URLs; private endpoints are read from existing cache files only.
The workflow bundle ID is `com.aqsnow.alfred.spotify`. Its icon is reused from the Spotify desktop app; Spotify owns the icon and associated trademarks.
On first launch, the workflow imports data, privately saved credentials, and cache from `com.aqsnow.alfred-spotify`, or from the original `io.nhooyr.alfred-spotify` build if the newer source is absent. It reuses authorization, the SQLite index, and cached artwork without overwriting newer files or deleting the originals. Old sessions and lock files are skipped. This happens once, so clearing your connection later cannot restore the old authorization. A cleared connection in the newest source also takes precedence over any older authorization.
Credentials copied from your old workflow are kept in the workflow’s private data folder and fill empty settings on the first launch after import. They are never included in the source repository or exported workflow.
## Development
```sh PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v ./build.sh ```
Source: `src/alfred_spotify`. The native UI and workflow metadata are generated by `scripts/build.py`. `workflow/Spotify.alfredui/run` resolves Python without depending on shell startup files. Tests use temporary data and synthetic cache entries; they do not control playback, log in, or modify Spotify’s files.
UI reference: [Alfred Music Mini Player](https://www.alfredapp.com/help/features/music/) and [Alfred UI](https://www.alfredapp.com/help/alfredui/). Cache format reference: [Chromium Simple Cache](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/net/+/refs/heads/main/disk_cache/simple/simple_entry_format.h). Metadata field reference: [librespot metadata.proto](https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot/blob/dev/protocol/proto/metadata.proto).
